title: Minimality of the scheme-theoretic closure
statement:
The scheme-theoretic closure is the smallest closed subscheme of $Y$
through which $a$ factors: it factors through every such closed subscheme,
and the comparison is unique over $Y$.

proof.text:
This is [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-universal] applied to the immersion
$a$, together with
[def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure].

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $g\colon T\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and let
$z\colon Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion with ideal sheaf
$\mathcal I_Z$. Then $\mathcal I_Z\subseteq\ker(g)$, i.e.
$\operatorname{SIm}(g)\subseteq Z$, if and only if $g$ factors through $z$,
and the factorization $T\to Z$ is then unique. Thus $\operatorname{SIm}(g)$
is the smallest closed subscheme of $Y$ through which $g$ factors; in
particular the scheme-theoretic closure of a locally closed subscheme is the
smallest closed subscheme containing it.

proof.text:
If $\mathcal I_Z\subseteq\ker(g)$, then
[lemma-nagata-scheme-image-universal] gives the comparison
$c_{g,Z}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(g)\to Z$ with
$z\circ c_{g,Z}=g_{\mathrm{im}}$, so $h=c_{g,Z}\circ g^{\mathrm{im}}$
satisfies $z\circ h=g_{\mathrm{im}}\circ g^{\mathrm{im}}=g$. Conversely, if
$z\circ h=g$, every local section of $\mathcal I_Z$ maps to zero in
$z_*\mathcal O_Z$, hence in $g_*\mathcal O_T$; since $\mathcal I_Z$ is
quasi-coherent and $\ker(g)$ is the largest quasi-coherent ideal in the
kernel of $\mathcal O_Y\to g_*\mathcal O_T$, we get
$\mathcal I_Z\subseteq\ker(g)$. Uniqueness of the factorization holds
because the closed immersion $z$ is a monomorphism.
